headline: Binance hack estimated at $5.6-6.3 billion, blamed on North Korean hackers
summary: Outlets reported a major Binance crypto hack, with early estimates of $5.8 billion rising to a widely repeated $6.3 billion figure, while Tom's Hardware put the loss at $5.6 billion. Investigators and multiple outlets linked the theft to a DevOps engineer's compromised laptop and attributed it to North Korean hackers, including the group TraderTraitor. Binance said it would cover losses and moved to freeze stolen assets, though only part of the total had been recovered as of these reports.

claims.statement: Binance paused withdrawals and investigated a major hack, with early reports estimating up to $5.8 billion stolen.

sources.quote: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto

claims.statement: Later reports from most outlets settled on roughly $6.3 billion stolen, calling it the largest-ever crypto heist.

claims.statement: Tom's Hardware reported the theft at $5.6 billion, a different figure than most other outlets' $6.3 billion.

claims.statement: Binance and investigators linked the theft to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop.

claims.statement: Binance said it would cover customer losses and moved to freeze stolen assets, with only part of the total recovered so far.

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets give different dollar estimates for the theft: $5.8 billion in Bleepingcomputer's early report, $6.3 billion in most later accounts, and $5.6 billion in Tom's Hardware's report.
